title: 700. Redundant Connection II

examples.explanation: Removing [2,3] leaves every node with one parent and no cycle.
Removing [4,1] breaks the directed cycle while keeping the tree rooted.
Node 1 has two parents; dropping the earlier of the conflicting edges fixes both issues.

hints: A valid rooted tree gives every node exactly one parent; find a node with two parents if it exists.
Try removing each of the two conflicting edges and check whether the rest is acyclic with union-find.
With no double parent, the answer is the edge that closes a cycle, i.e. the last edge joining already-connected nodes.
